transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is that I just can't seem to shake this heavy mix of fear and guilt. It's like I'm tense all day, just waiting for something else to go wrong, and... I just keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened.
Can you tell me if there was a specific event or situation that happened which you feel is connected to this fear and guilt you're experiencing now?

Yeah, there is. Um... this has all been going on for about four months now. It started ever since my husband had a fall. We were doing a repair on our porch, and he fell... so, yeah, that's what it's connected to.
Since the fall happened, have you found yourself re-living the event through unwanted memories or flashbacks, even when you don’t want to?

Yeah, I do. It happens at work a lot. I'll just be... measuring a railing or something, or I'll hear a ladder scrape, and out of nowhere I can see him falling. It's like it's happening right in front of me all over again. My stomach just drops, and my hands get all shaky... it just comes on even when I'm just trying to do my job.
Since the fall, have you found yourself avoiding certain places, activities, or people that remind you of what happened?

Yeah, I have. Um... at work, I've actually started turning down jobs if they involve inspecting raised porches or second-story decks. I just... I don't want to be up there right now. And at home, I find excuses not to talk about the repair we were doing. I really try not to even look at the spot where he fell if I can help it.
Have you noticed that your feelings of guilt and fear have remained constant since the fall, or do they come and go?

Um... they're pretty constant, honestly. That's actually a big part of what brings me in. I just can't seem to shake this heavy mix of fear and guilt. It's like... I'm just tense all day, waiting for something else to go wrong. And I keep blaming myself for not stopping what happened, so it really just stays with me all the time.
Since the fall, have you had trouble relaxing, difficulty sleeping, or found yourself being easily startled?

Yeah, sleep has been pretty tough. Most nights I just lie there replaying things in my head for an hour or two before I can drift off. And even when I finally do fall asleep, I don't stay asleep. I wake up at every little creak the house makes, or I'll wake up from these dreams where... where I just hear him hit the ground again. It's really hard to get any rest.
Have these feelings of fear and guilt made it hard for you to function normally, like at work or with your relationships at home?

Yeah, mostly at work. I mean, I'm still working, but... my inspection reports take a lot longer now because I just keep second-guessing myself on them. And like I mentioned, I've been turning down any jobs with elevated decks or porches. I used to handle those without any hesitation at all, but now I just avoid them. So it's definitely making my job a lot harder right now.
Do you feel that your guilt and fear are directly connected to what happened to your husband, or do these feelings seem more general and not tied to any specific cause?

Um, it's definitely connected directly to what happened to him. I didn't feel this way before his fall. The guilt is entirely about not stopping it, and the fear just... it all goes back to that day. It's not just some general feeling out of nowhere, it's very much tied to the accident.
